evidence: Reusable presets are implemented only as a bounded user-level input layer that flattens into the existing CLROOM skill/resource/environment/provider-argv path and the same ResolvedLaunch; no second launcher or provider settings framework is introduced.

Provider inference is fail-closed and based on the intersection of explicitly permitted providers across selected presets; direct CLI provider selection remains authoritative only when every selected preset permits it.

Preset file parsing, selected preset count, list/argv sizes and total resolved composition are bounded before provider birth; stored secret-shaped/auth-lifecycle/CLROOM-control/argv-terminator inputs are refused.

Focused preset unit and CLI regressions cover missing/malformed config, default/none/ordered composition, provider ambiguity/intersection, exact resource precedence, explicit CLI skill replacement, environment-name validation, zero-auth/auth lifecycle refusal and CLROOM-control smuggling.
A dedicated aggregate-resolution negative proves individually valid preset fragments cannot combine into an unbounded resolved launch budget.
Existing required CI, CodeQL, fuzz, dependency and discovery jobs remain in the exact-candidate topology; provider/runtime and performance gates remain separately required before release acceptance.
The product source version advances from 0.5.0 to 0.6.0 but no runtime/build dependency is added, removed or version-changed; serde_yaml already existed before this release.
Cargo.lock and fuzz/Cargo.lock changes are package-identity synchronization only; Dependency Review remains required.
The post-v0.5 delta adds required documentation freshness, discovery metadata/routing, link-graph and problem-language vector validation to ordinary CI.

Preset behavior itself is exercised by the existing Rust all-target test topology rather than a parallel ad-hoc workflow; release acceptance additionally requires qualified-target performance and current-provider evidence recorded below.

The public Release Contract now makes reusable preset closure durable: single resolution authority, bounded local parse, deterministic precedence, explicit machine-schema evolution, no provider-owned widening and qualified-target performance evidence.

The existing release system still requires exact candidate whole-release content review, provider freshness/registry integrity, PR-candidate runtime rehearsal, accepted-main exact-byte staging, exact public preview, guarded tag/publish actions and public-install verification.
v0.6 release acceptance is explicitly blocked until the current stable Codex/Claude tuple is refreshed and qualified and preset-resolution performance evidence is captured on qualified Apple Silicon.
README and canonical docs add one answer-first presets page plus native-alternative routing that distinguishes CLROOM launch intent from Codex profiles and Claude settings/subagent controls.

Problem-index/llms/glossary/use-case/runner surfaces route reusable-preset language to canonical answers without creating per-keyword duplicate pages; the post-v0.5 discovery hardening preserves canonical/link/metadata/privacy/trust coherence.

Machine inspection schema advances explicitly to clroom.resolved-launch.v2 when preset provenance is added; provider argv values, environment values, private paths and secret material remain non-claims.

near_misses.failure_mode: Adding top-level preset provenance to JSON inspection while retaining clroom.resolved-launch.v1 would silently change a versioned human/AI machine contract under an existing schema identifier.
near_misses.durable_control: Resolved launch inspection now advances explicitly to clroom.resolved-launch.v2; unit serialization regression asserts the v2 identifier and preset provenance, and the Release Contract requires explicit schema-version evolution for future JSON shape changes.

near_misses.failure_mode: A preset file validated as small by metadata could grow before an unbounded whole-file read, turning a nominal size limit into an allocation/TOCTOU weakness.
near_misses.durable_control: Preset loading opens the file and reads through a MAX_FILE_BYTES+1 bounded reader, then refuses overflow; the Release Contract requires read bounds independent of prior filesystem metadata.

near_misses.failure_mode: Several individually bounded preset categories could compose into a total launch larger than the intended resolved-work budget.
near_misses.durable_control: The resolver now computes one aggregate resolved-item budget before synthesis and fails with CLROOM_PRESET_RESOLUTION_TOO_LARGE; a focused CLI regression selects five individually valid provider-argv layers whose total exceeds the cap.

near_misses.failure_mode: Stored literal provider argv could shift auth lifecycle commands or smuggle launcher-owned preset/resource/skill/environment controls past the intended precedence and zero-auth boundary.
near_misses.durable_control: Stored argv refuses credential-shaped material, auth/login/logout, argv terminator and CLROOM-owned controls; execution re-enters the existing resource/skill/env/conflict/zero-auth path and focused negative tests cover these cases.

near_misses.failure_mode: Search engines can continue surfacing historical ewgenij87snwork.github.io CLROOM Pages URLs while the canonical project site is y-sor.github.io/clean-room-launcher, confusing users despite correct new-site canonicals.
near_misses.durable_control: Track separately in public Issue #125 and private discovery research state. Do not recreate the old product repository because GitHub repository-transfer redirects would be destroyed; investigate only controllable redirect/old-host/search-console surfaces under their own gates.

artifact_capability_gates.requirement: Exact PR candidate must pass focused and full Rust/CLI regressions for preset schema/bounds, default/none/ordered layering, provider inference, resource precedence, CLI skill replacement, env-name handling, literal provider argv safety, aggregate composition cap and clroom.resolved-launch.v2 inspection provenance.

Benchmark 0/1/10/100/1000-preset resolution plus representative saved skill-set use on qualified macOS Apple Silicon; record measurements and block if representative 100-preset resolution exceeds the accepted <=10 ms p95 budget unless the contract is explicitly revised.

Refresh current stable Codex and Claude versions from authoritative package/release inputs, verify registry/package/native integrity, synchronize shipped qualification constants and public claims, then rerun exact-provider clean/selective/composed rehearsals. Stale 0.160.0/2.1.289 evidence cannot qualify a later current tuple.

Re-run current native-alternative and adjacent-solution review; keep CLROOM presets limited to top-level clean/selective launch intent, map distinct user/problem language to canonical answers, and preserve truthful native-provider routing and search-migration residue classification.
Materialize and independently review exact v0.6.0 release facts, notes and publish preview; bind semantic public-claim PASS and exact bytes before any protected tag.
After separate Owner publish approval, use only the canonical guarded publish helper with exact Draft/tag/payload guards and authoritative reconciliation.
Verify Latest Release, releases/latest/download assets, attestations and isolated public installation before reporting PUBLIC_INSTALL_VERIFIED.

product_outcome: Ship v0.6.0 as a durable reusable CLROOM launch-intent layer over the existing ResolvedLaunch: users can save bounded provider-specific top-level clean/selective composition once and reuse it without duplicating provider-native profile/settings/orchestration systems, weakening zero-auth/qualification policy, or expanding unsupported resource capabilities.

contract_evolution_review.rationale: v0.6.0 introduces persistent user-authored launch composition that can affect provider selection, resources, global skills, admitted environment names and provider argv before provider birth. This creates new parsing, precedence, resource-budget, zero-auth and machine-inspection compatibility surfaces, so the release contract expands to require one bounded resolver authority, explicit schema evolution, focused negative closure and qualified-target performance evidence. The post-v0.5 discovery hardening also makes current provider/native alternatives, semantic problem-language coverage and rendered public-state coherence durable release obligations.
promoted_controls: one strict user-level clroom.presets.v1 file and no project/team/remote preset trust layer
preset flattening into the same existing direct-CLI and ResolvedLaunch authority rather than a second launcher/settings framework
bounded file read plus bounded schema/count/list/argv/selected-preset and aggregate resolved-composition budgets
fail-closed provider intersection/inference and deterministic default/none/ordered/explicit-CLI precedence
stored provider argv refusal for secret-shaped values, auth lifecycle commands, CLROOM-owned controls and argv terminator
explicit clroom.resolved-launch.v2 JSON schema for preset provenance with sensitive/private values still redacted
qualified-target preset-resolution performance evidence before release acceptance
current provider/native-alternative/discovery research refresh before release acceptance
